D9’s burial is at a recessed ledge at the base / side of the older shaft. This cannot be substituted for tombs at a separately defined pit mouth.

value.dating_basis: type comparison; no grave-associated dating finds in III 173–174

observations.note: Kenyon assigns the on-tell graves to the first century CE by grave-type comparison. There are no offerings in this scope and no dated jointly accessible grave/pit-mouth interval.
Numerous later pits occupy much of the northern trench end. Their individual mouths have no national-datum position.
observations.reference_frame: Trench II / Site O local frame

observations.note: The phase-lxxvii quarry pits cut phase-lxxvi graves and are rubble-filled. They have no secure absolute date; later-than-grave alone is not an early-window failure.
The pits truncate the graves and belong to later phase lxxvii, after grave phase lxxvi. This rejects same-phase construction only; it does not settle later joint accessibility.
Published truncation establishes sequence, not whether a usable later opening and surviving graves were jointly accessible within an early window.

On this named crypt-basin/spring assignment, the church is at the western foot and the spring southwest of the tell. This conditional crosswalk contradicts east-of-tell; it does not locate Kallai’s separate pool.
observations.reference_frame: Published qualitative church/spring/tell crosswalk; no validated bearing

observations.note: The basin was beneath a Byzantine church crypt; the church was later destroyed. The basin itself has no separate construction date or early-use interval.
Kallai’s original pp. 172–173 remain unread and the reported rock-cut pool remains unlocated. HA 76 p. 19 describes settlement excavation and supplies no pool or bearing.
No dated pool phase or physical crosswalk to the crypt basin is established; Kallai’s native pool pages remain unread.
Dhahr Mirzbaneh’s shaft tombs are documented north/NNE of the tell and attributed to Intermediate Bronze / Middle Bronze. Their ancient mouths and later accessibility are unobserved here.

value.attributed_date: Intermediate Bronze / Middle Bronze; later accessible use unknown

observations.note: Bronze Age construction does not establish or exclude survival/accessibility in the early Roman window. There is no dated pit-mouth relation to this group.
Roman–Byzantine dams and aqueducts are reported at Kh. Samiya south/SE of the tell. No surveyed contact to Kallai’s pool or the church crypt basin is established.
The inspected Kh. Yanun site record describes no pit/cistern/tomb. This is report coverage, not an archaeological absence; a pit role remains unassigned.
Rock-cut dividing pillar reported on p. 63; its cutting date is unresolved.
A pillar does not decide the retained platform/terrace reading.

modules.title: Landmark relationships
modules.summary: Compare finite Koḥlit assignments against separate edition-based relations and use windows. Retain each failed and unresolved branch.
modules.scope: Exploratory Entry 11 / Entry 60 pilot at Jericho, Ein Samiya and the reading-dependent Yanun route. This selected roster cannot establish regional discrimination or identification.

results.title: Jericho historical basin + NS1 · Milik: north-facing opening · 50 BCE–70 CE
results.claim: The selected physical features satisfy this exploratory Entry 11 / Entry 60 relationship branch within the selected use window.

checks.label: Pool east of the Koḥlit anchor
checks.detail: The historical basin is documented at the spring on the tell’s eastern foot. This is a qualitative source relation; no basin-to-anchor surveyed bearing is asserted.

checks.label: Pool accessible in the selected early window
checks.detail: The irregular basin is observed in nineteenth-century records; its construction and early accessible-use interval are unknown. Do not backdate it from the adjacent ancient curved wall.

checks.label: Ancient pool has the specified northern corner
checks.detail: Historical basin descriptions and modern walls do not define a dated ancient northern-corner datum.

checks.label: Pit north of the Koḥlit anchor
checks.detail: NS1 is reported on the camp outskirts toward Khirbet Mefjar, north of the tell. No plan or surveyed cistern-mouth position was made.

checks.label: Pit accessible in the selected early window

checks.label: Defined side opening faces north
checks.detail: No defined side opening and source-controlled facing direction are supplied; a vertical shaft is not assigned an azimuth.

checks.label: Tombs at the pit mouth
checks.detail: Graves and a pit in the same northern sector do not establish individual tomb mouths at this pit mouth. No metric proximity tolerance is invented.

checks.label: Pit mouth and graves jointly accessible
checks.detail: Independent feature dates and relative succession do not establish contemporaneous accessible mouths within the selected early window.

results.title: Later quarry pits and earlier north-slope graves
results.claim: The phase-lxxvii quarry pits were constructed in the same stratigraphic phase as the phase-lxxvi graves.

checks.label: Quarry pits and graves share construction phase
checks.detail: The pits truncate the graves and belong to later phase lxxvii, after grave phase lxxvi. This rejects same-phase construction only; it does not settle later joint accessibility.

unknowns: Whether later openings and surviving graves were jointly accessible within either early window remains unknown.

supplementary_graph.note: The northern Koḥlit link is restored and north may attach to the cistern/pillar relation. NS1 is not automatically the great cistern with a northern pillar.
Puech restores a pool destination. Koḥlit association is contextual and equating this destination to Entry 11’s pool is a separate unverified alias hypothesis.
Eastern selects among pits; no second pit datum is defined. A north-of-site relation cannot resolve eastern among pits. Allegro’s no-place-name variant remains outside this core pilot.

limits: All inputs were already exposed in prior project work; none is an unused prediction or an independent confirmatory test.
The finite roster is selected for implementation and does not enumerate all Koḥlit proposals, regional pools, shafts or caves. Regional eligibility and denominator remain unknown.
Direction checks use explicitly attributed qualitative source statements or marked inference. They are not measured bearings, geographic outlines or tolerance-calibrated fits.
Separate construction phases can overlap in later usable states; relative pit/grave sequence does not establish or disprove early joint accessibility.
Known historical photographs cannot backdate the irregular basin or replace the securely 1898 reservoir with an ancient state.
Edition branches, Koḥlit anchors, pool/shaft identities and modern geographic positions remain separate hypotheses. Unknowns are never scored as misses.

Opening azimuth, mouth proximity, great-cistern identity, pillar position, conduit-to-pool identity and all phase-specific measuring datums remain unresolved. No new distances or deposits are generated.
The module imports source pointers, not source images; original reuse limits and parked acquisition remain unchanged.

limits.candidate_selection: Three previously examined comparators, not a regional census or a ranked sample.
limits.geometry: No surveyed individual-mouth world coordinates, true bearings or deposit points.
limits.confirmation: All source material was already exposed. No unused prediction is certified.
limits.claims: Reported feature compatibility, ancient feature phase and possible target geometry are separate. No deposit existence, survival, rarity or identification confidence is scored.

semantics.compatible: Every required reported predicate in this branch is supplied; exploratory compatibility only.
semantics.contradicted: At least one required predicate has a positive incompatible observation in an eligible frame/phase.
semantics.unknown: At least one required predicate lacks an eligible observation, with no positive contradiction.
semantics.mixed: Retained branches have different outcomes; all remain visible and none is selected as a candidate score.
semantics.unit: Three 0.40/0.50/0.60 m cubit sensitivity samples produce 1.20/1.50/1.80 m conditional distance; they never define mouth size.

modules.title: Historical feature states
modules.summary: Compare recorded remains with proposed ancient configurations and retain the missing date, datum and access observations.
modules.scope: Exploratory IV/17 and Tell es-Sultan pilots using already inspected records. Native source geometry has no geographic registration. Relative sequence, contemporaneous accessibility and feature identity are separate claims.

obligations.label: Other Ain Duq / Doq water-system notices
obligations.detail: Existing coverage notice is sector-level; the relation between spring-sector installations and Quruntul/Doq source features is unresolved.
obligations.next_observation: An individual source/locus crosswalk and feature-specific dates/contacts.

obligations.label: Doq numbered cisterns1-9
obligations.detail: Amit1989 Fig.7 p.226 supplies nine numbered outlines; the p.227 table reports dimensions/capacities for1-9. These remain a source-defined group, with no verified one-to-one catalogue crosswalk or entry29 datum. Plaster, later reuse and source construction attribution remain distinct.
obligations.next_observation: Crosswalk each numbered cistern and its hydraulic stage to the retained catalogue notice; survey the selected ancient wall/terminal/surface.

obligations.label: Doq small pool remains beside the aqueduct
obligations.detail: Amit1989 p.225 distinguishes western and eastern remains. The western basin is cut/built and has three partly preserved sides, possible fourth-wall remains and approximately1.5x1.5m dimensions; only the eastern sidewall/plaster remains of the other. Short-term-use interpretation is the author's. Whole-basin excavation status and phase-controlled contacts are unknown.
obligations.next_observation: Individual pool identities, ancient full outlines, dated functions and observed inlet/outlet contacts; keep them separate from numbered cisterns.

obligations.label: Doq high filled cistern notice10
obligations.detail: Amit1989 p.227 reports notice10 near the summit filled with collapse and interprets a different later/monastery context. No visible ancient basin/contact geometry is supplied for entry29.
obligations.next_observation: Its individual fabric/phase, ancient shape and water connection, with safe observation/detection coverage; period attribution cannot supply an earlier layout.

obligations.label: Doq map notice11
obligations.detail: Amit1989 Fig.2 p.224 plots number11 with the cistern symbol. It is outside the numbered1-9 outlines and dimensions table; individual dimensions, phase, contacts, preservation and catalogue crosswalk remain unknown. A map symbol establishes a source notice only.
obligations.next_observation: An original feature-description/locus crosswalk, dated construction/contact and measured ancient face/surface; neither silence nor the map symbol proves eligibility.

obligations.label: Estate Na'aran branch flow-control basin
obligations.detail: Netzer1989 p.277 reports a2.2x2.2m basin below the steep northern branch, interpreted as reducing flow velocity. A numbered-locus and existing-roster crosswalk is unresolved.
obligations.next_observation: A source crosswalk and dated basin-wall contacts before treating this as an additional independent basin.

obligations.label: Nuseib Uweishira ritual-bath notice
obligations.detail: Netzer2006 p.207 reports a ritual bath among meagre Herodian-period finds below a Byzantine monastery; the Hasmonean initial-construction suggestion concerns the site and remains an inference. The source places the summit north of Wadi Qelt's mouth, about3km south ofDoq, withCypros less than1km to its south. Basin locus, contact, dimensions and excavation coverage are unknown; no equivalence to Penthucla or another catalogue notice is inferred.
obligations.next_observation: An original bath-locus/phase/plan crosswalk, dated water contact and footprint; regional inclusion remains conditional until a boundary is justified.
